Hi Marissa —

Thanks again for the draft MSA. We're attaching a redline (FinServe_MSA_redline_v2.pdf) with a couple of sticking points on dispute resolution that came up in procurement and legal review:

- FinServe prefers arbitration for most disputes (we proposed AAA/JAMS language).
- Procurement is pushing back on a blanket carveout for injunctive relief — they want a clearer temporary-measures protocol and a limited waiver model.

Two asks: can Redwood confirm (1) whether you can accept an injunctive-relief carveout that explicitly preserves the right to arbitrate afterward, and (2) whether you have a preferred governing law / forum for temporary measures? Our negotiations team is trying to avoid broad forum-selection language.

Attaching the redline and a short note explaining our position. Happy to jump on a call today or tomorrow; Gina and I are available after 2pm PT.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Baker

Tom —

Appreciate the redline. Short answer: yes, we're open to a narrowly tailored injunctive-relief carveout so long as it: (a) preserves arbitration for monetary and non-emergency claims, and (b) includes an expedited preservation/notice protocol.

Two quick proposals to unblock:
- Call: Lauren (CC'd) can take a 30-min slot tomorrow 10–11am PT or 3–4pm PT to align commercial/legal.
- Temporary language: would you accept a clause along the lines of — "Notwithstanding the agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek interim injunctive or other equitable relief in the courts of the State of Washington; seeking such relief shall not constitute a waiver of the right to compel arbitration for the underlying dispute." (We can refine).

If that looks reasonable, I'll loop in Karthik (legal) to provide firm redline language and an emergency-relief SOP we prefer.

Best,

Marissa / Lauren —

Thanks — I've reviewed FinServe's redline and drafted recommended language we think will be commercially acceptable while protecting Redwood's arbitration rights. Key points:

1) Governing law: State of Washington (no application of conflict-of-law rules).
2) Arbitration: Binding arbitration governed by the Federal Arbitration Act, administered by JAMS, located in King County (Seattle).
3) Injunctive-relief carveout (recommended):
   - "Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek temporary or preliminary injunctive or other equitable relief in the state or federal courts located in King County, Washington (the 'Injunction Courts') to preserve the status quo or protect confidential information, intellectual property, or the safety of systems and data. Such application for injunctive relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the right to arbitrate any other dispute, and the parties shall promptly submit the underlying dispute to arbitration in accordance with Section [X]."
4) Emergency procedure: short preservation notice (24 hours where practicable) to Redwood Legal with an explanation of the emergency and proposed relief; if notice is impossible given timing, parties may proceed but must provide notice as soon as reasonably practicable.
5) Interim discovery: specify limited expedited discovery (depositions/evidence preservation) tied to injunctive motions to reduce scope creep.

Suggested single-sentence redline to add to the MSA (clean copy for insertion):
"The parties agree that, notwithstanding any agreement to arbitrate, either party may seek interim injunctive or equitable relief in the state or federal courts located in King County, Washington, and taking such action shall not constitute a waiver of any right to arbitrate remaining claims."

Why this should fly: it addresses FinServe's procurement team's desire for a local forum for emergency relief, while keeping arbitration as the primary ICP for monetary disputes. If FinServe insists on a different neutral forum for arbitration (e.g., New York or JAMS in another city), that's a commercial talk — we prefer Seattle for operational simplicity.

I've attached a short text file with the proposed insertion and an example emergency-notice template (proposed_injunction_text.txt).

—Karthik

Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Karthik / Marissa —

Thanks for the clear proposal and the template. That language is largely acceptable to FinServe's legal team. Two quick items before we finalize:

1) Forum flexibility: we prefer the emergency forum to be "state or federal courts in King County, Washington OR the Western District of Washington" to be explicit about federal options.
2) Arbitration venue: JAMS in Seattle is fine, but procurement asked whether a clause can state "JAMS (seat: Seattle), with the arbitrator permitted to hear procedural pre-arbitral matters remotely."

If those tweaks look good, we'll accept and sign. Attaching an updated order form draft for execution (orderform_draft.docx) and can route the final MSA via DocuSign.

Tom
